entities.title: Hillhurst Sunnyside Farmers' Market
entities.summary: A year-round Wednesday farmers' market run by the Hillhurst Sunnyside Community Association.
entities.description: Weekly community farmers' market at the Hillhurst Sunnyside Community Centre, running year-round every Wednesday afternoon. Local produce, food vendors and makers, and a community social gathering as much as a market.

images.alt: Hillhurst Sunnyside Farmers Market fresh produce and community stalls

image.alt: Hillhurst Sunnyside Farmers Market fresh produce and community stalls

entities.title: Bridgeland-Riverside Farmers' Market
entities.summary: A seasonal Thursday farmers' market outside the BRCA Hall in Bridgeland.
entities.description: Seasonal community farmers' market outside the Bridgeland-Riverside Community Association hall, running Thursday afternoons through the summer and early fall market season.

images.alt: Bridgeland-Riverside Farmers Market outside BRCA Hall overlooking the city

image.alt: Bridgeland-Riverside Farmers Market outside BRCA Hall overlooking the city

entities.title: Calgary Farmers' Market West
entities.summary: A year-round market and food hall with Alberta growers, makers and places to eat.
entities.description: Calgary Farmers' Market West is open year-round with local produce, prepared food, Alberta-made goods, a food hall and family amenities. Official hours are Wednesday through Saturday from 9 a.m. to 7 p.m. and Sunday from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m.
entities.parking: Free parking in market lots and on nearby streets.

images.alt: Calgary Farmers Market West local stalls and food hall

image.alt: Calgary Farmers Market West local stalls and food hall

entities.title: Calgary Farmers' Market South
entities.summary: Calgary's year-round south market for local produce, prepared food and Alberta makers.
entities.description: Calgary Farmers' Market South is open year-round from Thursday through Sunday, with local growers, food vendors, handmade goods, a food hall and family amenities.
entities.parking: Free parking in market lots and on nearby streets.

images.alt: Calgary Farmers Market South community produce and Alberta makers

image.alt: Calgary Farmers Market South community produce and Alberta makers

entities.title: Crossroads Market
entities.summary: A year-round weekend market with fresh food, local vendors, antiques and a food court.
entities.description: Crossroads Market has welcomed Calgarians since 1987. The indoor market is open year-round every Friday, Saturday and Sunday from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m., with fresh food, local vendors, crafts, antiques and a food court.

images.alt: Crossroads Market food stalls, crafts, and antiques

image.alt: Crossroads Market food stalls, crafts, and antiques

entities.title: Farmers & Makers Market at cSPACE
entities.summary: A Saturday market with local farms, food makers, artists, food trucks and live music.
entities.description: The nonprofit Calgary Earth Market Society runs this Alberta Approved Farmers' Market every Saturday during its outdoor season. The 2026 season runs May 23 through October 17 from 10 a.m. to 2 p.m. at cSPACE Marda Loop.

images.alt: Farmers and Makers Market at cSPACE Marda Loop with food trucks and music

image.alt: Farmers and Makers Market at cSPACE Marda Loop with food trucks and music

entities.title: Inglewood
entities.summary: Calgary’s oldest historic neighbourhood, packed with red-brick heritage, artisan shops, craft breweries, and river pathways.
entities.description: Established in 1875 alongside Fort Calgary, Inglewood is Calgary’s cultural and heritage cornerstone. 9th Avenue SE features independent record stores, boutique coffee roasters, vintage clothing emporiums, and renowned dining, all framed by the curve of the Bow River and the Inglewood Bird Sanctuary.

sources.name: City of Calgary Heritage & Inglewood BRZ

image.alt: Inglewood historic brick streetscape and Bow River bend

entities.title: Kensington
entities.summary: An energetic, tree-lined urban village across the river from downtown, centred on 10th Street NW and Kensington Road.
entities.description: Kensington is Calgary’s iconic pedestrian-friendly urban hub. Home to over 250 independent businesses, vibrant patios, indie cinema, and Riley Park, it acts as the primary northwest gateway across the Bow River via the Peace Bridge.

image.alt: Kensington 10th Street NW and Peace Bridge entrance

entities.title: Beltline
entities.summary: Calgary’s vibrant inner-city core, buzzing with high-density dining, 17th Ave retail, historic Central Memorial Park, and public art.
entities.description: Positioned immediately south of the Canadian Pacific mainline and downtown towers, the Beltline is Calgary’s most dense and bustling urban neighborhood. Renowned for 17th Avenue SW (the Red Mile), the annual BUMP festival mural galleries, and Central Memorial Park.

sources.name: Beltline Urban Development & City of Calgary

image.alt: Beltline 17th Avenue SW and Central Memorial Park

entities.title: Bridgeland-Riverside
entities.summary: A sun-drenched escarpment village known for Italian bakeries, Murdock Park panoramic skyline views, and riverside parklets.
entities.description: Nestled between the bluff hills and the north bank of the Bow River, Bridgeland is renowned for its welcoming European café culture along 1st Avenue NE, the scenic 4th Street flyover connection to downtown, and extensive community programming centered at the BRCA hall.

image.alt: Bridgeland 1st Avenue NE and skyline views from Murdoch Park

entities.title: Marda Loop
entities.summary: Southwest Calgary’s favourite creative high street, featuring 33rd Avenue boutiques, cSPACE Marda Loop arts incubator, and lively patios.
entities.description: Taking its name from the historic Marda Theatre and the streetcar turnaround loop, Marda Loop has grown into a bustling pedestrian destination anchored along 33rd and 34th Avenues SW. Cultural life converges at cSPACE King Edward, a heritage sandstone school transformed into studios and weekend farmers markets.

image.alt: Marda Loop 33rd Avenue pedestrian streetscape

entities.title: Bowness
entities.summary: A storied Bow Valley river town incorporated into Calgary, celebrated for Bowness Park lagoon, mature cottonwood groves, and small-town spirit.
entities.description: Once an independent town destination connected by streetcar, Bowness maintains an unmistakable pride of place along the Bow River. Home to Bowness Park’s iconic boat lagoon and winter ice trail, Main Street (Bowness Road) local shops, and direct access to Shouldice Park.

sources.name: Bowness Community Association & City of Calgary

image.alt: Bowness Park lagoon and pathway bridge

entities.title: Ramsay
entities.summary: Hilltop heritage community overlooking the confluence, featuring red-brick alleyways, artisan workshops, and sweeping Stampede Park vistas.
entities.description: Directly east of the Elbow River and south of Inglewood, Ramsay climbs the Scotsman’s Hill escarpment. Renowned for its preserved historic workers’ cottages, active laneway tool shares, independent design studios, and the iconic city panorama from Scotsman’s Hill.

image.alt: Ramsay historic cottage streetscape and skyline ridge

entities.title: A Day Along the Bow River
entities.summary: From Harvie Passage to the Peace Bridge: 12 km of world-class riverfront paths, public art, and island parklets.
entities.description: The Bow River is the spine of Calgary life. This curated itinerary guides you along paved shared paths from the whitewater rapids at Harvie Passage through St. Patrick’s Island, past Prince’s Island Park, and beneath Santiago Calatrava’s Peace Bridge.

image.alt: Peace Bridge and Bow River trail skyline view

entities.introduction: Calgary boasts the largest paved urban pathway network in North America. This route showcases the city at its most natural and connected.
entities.methodology: Ground-truthed by CalgaryWatch editors with accessibility notes, bike parking locations, and seasonal riverflow telemetry.

entities.title: Calgary Farmers’ Markets & Artisan Food Halls
entities.summary: Where to find Alberta sourdough, organic foothills produce, local apiaries, and slow-morning market breakfasts.
entities.description: From century-old Crossroads Market to modern community popups at Hillhurst Sunnyside, Bridgeland, and cSPACE Marda Loop, this guide maps Calgary’s best local food hubs.

image.alt: Calgary farmers market fresh produce and artisan food stalls

entities.introduction: Every quadrant of Calgary has its own weekend market ritual. Here is where the city comes to taste what our province grows.
entities.methodology: Curated and verified with published market coordinators, seasonal calendars, and transit accessibility notes.

entities.title: Historic Laneways & Craft Coffee of Inglewood and Ramsay
entities.summary: Discover red-brick carriage houses, roasteries, and independent record stores across Calgary’s oldest postal codes.
entities.description: A relaxed walking loop connecting 9th Avenue SE in Inglewood to the sandstone ridge of Ramsay. Enjoy specialty single-origin espresso, hidden courtyard bakeries, and century-old architectural character.

image.alt: Calgary historic brick laneway and cozy patio café

entities.introduction: Calgary’s historical character is best experienced on foot, where sandstone foundation blocks meet contemporary craft coffee.
entities.methodology: Vetted with Calgary heritage building registries and verified independently by local contributors.

entities.name: Rosso Coffee Roasters — Inglewood
entities.title: Rosso Coffee Roasters — Inglewood
entities.summary: Direct-trade coffee roasted right in SE Calgary, served alongside fresh sourdough pastries in a light-filled industrial brick room.
entities.description: A beloved Calgary institution since 2007. Rosso’s Inglewood outpost offers single-origin pour-overs, cold brew, and a welcoming meeting space for neighbours and Bow River cyclists.

image.alt: Rosso Coffee Roasters café patio on 9th Ave SE

images.alt: Rosso Coffee Roasters interior and espresso machine

entities.name: Higher Ground Café — Kensington
entities.title: Higher Ground Café — Kensington
entities.summary: A staple 10th Street NW gathering place serving 100% organic, fair-trade coffee and warm comfort meals until late.
entities.description: An anchor of Kensington for over twenty years. Features a fireplace, local art displays on brick walls, and late operating hours popular with university students and neighbours.

image.alt: Higher Ground Cafe on 10th Street NW Kensington

entities.name: cSPACE Marda Loop Creative Hub
entities.title: cSPACE Marda Loop Creative Hub
entities.summary: A historic sandstone school turned vibrant multi-disciplinary creative hub with galleries, studios, and weekend farmers markets.
entities.description: Preserving the historic 1912 King Edward School, cSPACE provides workspace for more than 30 artists, creative entrepreneurs, a community coffee shop, and regular indoor-outdoor artisan fairs.

image.alt: cSPACE Marda Loop sandstone schoolhouse and courtyard

entities.name: Luke’s Drug Mart — Bridgeland
entities.title: Luke’s Drug Mart — Bridgeland
entities.summary: Calgary’s oldest independent pharmacy, transformed into a cultural hub with specialty vinyl, soft serve ice cream, and espresso.
entities.description: Operating in Bridgeland since 1951, Luke’s blends a neighborhood pharmacy with curated vinyl records, specialty groceries, Four Barrel espresso, and seasonal soft serve.

sources.name: Luke’s Drug Mart Official & Bridgeland BRZ

image.alt: Luke’s Drug Mart in Bridgeland

images.alt: Luke’s Drug Mart shelves and vinyl records

entities.title: Love Letters From the Diaspora
entities.summary: An evening of storytelling, poetry and an open mic at Alcove Beltline.
entities.description: Presented by The Fourth Space. All ages welcome. The venue lists admission at $5 plus fees and tax; confirm ticket availability with the organizer. Steps are required to enter the Beltline venue.

image.alt: Love Letters From the Diaspora storytelling at Alcove Beltline

entities.title: Comics Workshop: Concept to Comic
entities.summary: Explore comic storytelling with Daniele and Gabe at Alcove Core.
entities.description: Registration is required. Admission is by donation. The organizer recommends ages 16 and over unless accompanied by a parent or guardian; all skill levels are welcome.

image.alt: Comics Workshop at Alcove Core in downtown Calgary
